questions.q: What does a PL/SQL package specification declare?
options: Nothing — specs are optional metadata with no effect
The full implementation code of every procedure and function
The public interface: procedure/function signatures and public variables callers can see
Only private helper procedures
questions.explain: The spec is the contract: what's visible to code outside the package. The body holds the actual implementation.

questions.q: A procedure defined in the package BODY but NOT listed in the package SPEC is:
options: Automatically public, since anything in the body is callable
A syntax error — every body routine must appear in the spec
Private — it cannot be called from outside the package
Only callable from T-SQL, never from PL/SQL
questions.explain: Spec/body separation lets you write private helper routines inside the body that are never exposed to callers.

questions.q: What happens when you rewrite a package BODY (e.g. fixing a bug) without changing the SPEC?
options: Every caller of the package must be rewritten too
The spec is automatically deleted and must be rebuilt
This is not possible; body and spec must always change together
You can recompile only the body — callers and the spec itself stay untouched
questions.explain: That's the whole point of the split: a stable public contract (spec) and a freely-changeable implementation (body).

questions.q: What is genuinely unique about a package-level variable like g_last_order_checked?
options: It behaves exactly like a T-SQL local variable declared inside a stored procedure
It resets to NULL after every single procedure call
It can only be read, never written, from inside the package
It persists for the life of the database session, across many separate calls, with no cleanup step required
questions.explain: A package variable is initialized once per session and keeps its value across calls for the rest of that session — a capability T-SQL has no built-in equivalent for.

questions.q: What's the closest thing T-SQL has to a PL/SQL package?
options: CREATE PACKAGE, which T-SQL supports with different syntax
T-SQL temp tables, which directly replace package variables
Grouping related stored procedures/functions in the same schema — an organizational convention, not a language feature with spec/body separation or private state
T-SQL schemas are functionally identical to Oracle packages, including session-persistent variables
questions.explain: T-SQL has nothing that replicates spec/body separation, private package members, or package-level session-persistent variables.
